statement:
Let \((x_n)\) be defined by \(x_1 \in \left(0, \tfrac{1}{2}\right)\) and \(x_{n+1} = 3x_n^2 - 2nx_n^3\) for all \(n \geq 1\).
a) Prove that \((x_n)\) converges to \(0\).
b) For each \(n \geq 1\), let \(y_n = x_1 + 2x_2 + \cdots + nx_n\). Prove that \((y_n)\) has a limit.

Find all functions \(f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) such that
\[f(x)f(y) = f(xy - 1) + yf(x) + xf(y)\]
for all \(x, y \in \mathbb{R}\).

Let \(\triangle ABC\) be a non-isosceles acute triangle with altitudes \(AD, BE, CF\) and orthocenter \(H\). Let \(I\) be the circumcenter of \(\triangle HEF\), and \(K, J\) the midpoints of \(BC, EF\) respectively. Line \(HJ\) meets \((I)\) again at \(G\), and \(GK\) meets \((I)\) at \(L \neq G\).
a) Prove that \(AL \perp EF\).
b) Let \(AL\) meet \(EF\) at \(M\). Line \(IM\) meets the circumcircle of \(\triangle IEF\) again at \(N\). Line \(DN\) meets \(AB, AC\) at \(P, Q\) respectively. Prove that \(PE, QF, AK\) are concurrent.

For an integer \(n \geq 2\), let \(s(n)\) be the sum of positive integers not exceeding \(n\) that are not relatively prime to \(n\).
a) Prove that \(s(n) = \dfrac{n}{2}(n + 1 - \varphi(n))\), where \(\varphi(n)\) is Euler's totient function.
b) Prove that there is no integer \(n \geq 2\) such that \(s(n) = s(n + 2021)\).

Let \(P(x) = a_{21}x^{21} + a_{20}x^{20} + \cdots + a_1 x + a_0\) where \(1011 \leq a_i \leq 2021\) for all \(i = 0, 1, \ldots, 21\). Suppose \(P(x)\) has an integer root and there exists a positive real number \(c\) such that \(|a_{k+2} - a_k| \leq c\) for all \(k = 0, 1, \ldots, 19\).
a) Prove that \(P(x)\) has exactly one integer root.
b) Prove that \(\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{10} (a_{2k+1} - a_{2k})^2 \leq 440c^2\).

A student divides 30 marbles into 5 numbered boxes \(1, 2, 3, 4, 5\) (a box may be empty).
a) How many ways are there to divide the marbles (two ways differ if any box has a different number of marbles)?
b) After dividing, the student paints the marbles with colors so that no 2 marbles in the same box share a color, and from any 2 boxes it is impossible to choose 8 marbles painted in exactly 4 colors. Prove that at least 10 colors are needed for every division.
c) Show a division for which exactly 10 colors suffice.

Let \(ABC\) be inscribed in circle \((O)\). Let \(D\) be the intersection of the tangents to \((O)\) at \(B\) and \(C\). The circle through \(A\) tangent to \(BC\) at \(B\) meets the median from \(A\) at \(G\). Lines \(BG, CG\) meet \(CD, BD\) at \(E, F\) respectively.
a) The line through the midpoints of \(BE\) and \(CF\) meets \(BF, CE\) at \(M, N\). Prove that \(A, D, M, N\) are concyclic.
b) Let \(AD, AG\) meet the circumcircles of \(\triangle DBC\) and \(\triangle GBC\) again at \(H, K\). The perpendicular bisectors of \(HK, HE, HF\) meet \(BC, CA, AB\) at \(R, P, Q\) respectively. Prove that \(R, P, Q\) are collinear.
